card.name: Small linking words mid-sentence
card.fires_on: Short linking words such as is, to, in, of, be or a comma, right after a noun phrase or modal verb in the middle of a clause. The next word is a predictable continuation, often a participle or a noun phrase.

modes.label: Verb after subject
modes.description: The verbs is or be (after can) that lead into a predicate adjective or participle.
modes.example: The APA style to be used<< is>> defined by the USQ Library's referencing

modes.label: Preposition or infinitive to
modes.description: The words to, in or of that start a phrase after a noun or participle.
modes.example: computers in which the present invention may be implemented. Distributed data processing system 100 contains network 102, which is the medium used<< to>> provide communications links between various devices and computers

modes.label: Comma after condition
modes.description: A comma closing an opening conditional clause before an instruction.
modes.example: WARNINGS: Keep out of reach of children. If pregnant or breast-feeding<<,>> ask a health care professional before use.

card.writes: It suppresses non-English word starts and promotes word-ending pieces such as s, es, ing and ed, so little useful output effect is clear.
card.plain: It fires on small glue words like is, to, in, of and be in the middle of ordinary sentences.
